The show takes the mental health angle very seriously by focusing on a man struggling with a dual identity and trying to find balance 
But it also covers deep childhood trauma, abuse, blocking out painful memories, and putting up emotional barriers 
More dark and supernatural concentration this time around in the world of the Marvel Cinematic Universe involving gods, the Afterlife, and balancing the scales of memories 
I really like the Moroccan influence this show presents with the music and the culture aspect 
This is a superhero that’s more unhinged much like DC’s Batman 
Director Mohamed Adib brings more of the Egyptology side of things mixing ‘Indiana Jones’, ‘Minority Report’, and ‘Jekyll & Hyde’ 
People don’t want to hear good news, they’d rather cling to their fears, doubts, are our minds easy to control because they’re broken or because they’re already falling apart?, a thought can’t be evil, maybe the difference between medicine and poison is a dosage given, even gods cannot interfere with man, it’s hard to take a life then trying to forget, finding peace with ourselves is key to moving forward

We also look back into Steven’s past and why his life turned out the way it did due to tragedy 
It’s actually really heartbreaking witnessing the birth of them both 
As to when this takes place in the MCU well that’s up for debate as there’s no clear timeline established so this show can be its own stand alone adventure
